`enum Key`<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.input.key` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [Key.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/input/key/Key.java)

A key of the keyboard, as the key events, the shortcuts and the key state name it.

## Description

A key event names a key by the layout of the user or by its place on the keyboard.
Each constant below names the key by what it types on a US keyboard.

Backend note: on LWJGL 2, JOID learns the key that a place types from the characters the user types, so a letter or punctuation key pressed with Shift or Alt before it was ever typed alone reports its place.

## Method details

<a id="Key-method-isDown"></a>

### isDown

`boolean isDown()` 

If `true`, a key that the layout names this way is held.
For a letter or punctuation key, it tests every held place that typed this key; for the other keys, it gives the same answer as `isPhysicalDown()`.

<a id="Key-method-isPhysicalDown"></a>

### isPhysicalDown

`boolean isPhysicalDown()` 

If `true`, the key at this place of a US QWERTY keyboard is held, whatever the layout names it.
It asks the window bridge, so it answers even for a key that no UI received.

<a id="Key-value-ESCAPE"></a>

### ESCAPE

`ESCAPE` 

The Escape key.
Unconsumed, it closes the top UI when that UI is closeable; a focused text field consumes it to lose the focus.

<a id="Key-value-ENTER"></a>

### ENTER

`ENTER` 

The Enter key of the main block.
A one-line text field submits on it; a multiline field starts a new line.

`NUMPAD_4` 

The `4` key of the numeric keypad.

<a id="Key-value-NUMPAD_5"></a>

### NUMPAD_5

`NUMPAD_5` 

The `5` key of the numeric keypad.

<a id="Key-value-NUMPAD_6"></a>

### NUMPAD_6

`NUMPAD_6` 

The `6` key of the numeric keypad.

<a id="Key-value-NUMPAD_7"></a>

### NUMPAD_7

`NUMPAD_7` 

The `7` key of the numeric keypad.

<a id="Key-value-NUMPAD_8"></a>

### NUMPAD_8

`NUMPAD_8` 

The `8` key of the numeric keypad.

<a id="Key-value-NUMPAD_9"></a>

### NUMPAD_9

`NUMPAD_9` 

The `9` key of the numeric keypad.

<a id="Key-value-NUMPAD_DECIMAL"></a>

### NUMPAD_DECIMAL

`NUMPAD_DECIMAL` 

The decimal point key of the numeric keypad.

<a id="Key-value-NUMPAD_DIVIDE"></a>

### NUMPAD_DIVIDE

`NUMPAD_DIVIDE` 

The divide key of the numeric keypad.

<a id="Key-value-NUMPAD_MULTIPLY"></a>

### NUMPAD_MULTIPLY

`NUMPAD_MULTIPLY` 

The multiply key of the numeric keypad.

<a id="Key-value-NUMPAD_SUBTRACT"></a>

### NUMPAD_SUBTRACT

`NUMPAD_SUBTRACT` 

The minus key of the numeric keypad.
In dev mode, with Ctrl or Alt, it zooms out a zoomable UI.

<a id="Key-value-NUMPAD_ADD"></a>

### NUMPAD_ADD

`NUMPAD_ADD` 

The plus key of the numeric keypad.
In dev mode, with Ctrl or Alt, it zooms in a zoomable UI.

<a id="Key-value-NUMPAD_ENTER"></a>

### NUMPAD_ENTER

`NUMPAD_ENTER` 

The Enter key of the numeric keypad; text fields treat it as `ENTER`.

<a id="Key-value-NUMPAD_EQUAL"></a>

### NUMPAD_EQUAL

`NUMPAD_EQUAL` 

The equal key of the numeric keypad.

<a id="Key-value-LEFT_SHIFT"></a>

### LEFT_SHIFT

`LEFT_SHIFT` 

The left Shift key; [`UI.isShiftKeyDown`](/reference/ui/ui/#UI-method-isShiftKeyDown) tests both Shift keys.

<a id="Key-value-LEFT_CONTROL"></a>

### LEFT_CONTROL

`LEFT_CONTROL` 

The left Control key; [`UI.isCtrlKeyDown`](/reference/ui/ui/#UI-method-isCtrlKeyDown) tests both Control keys.

<a id="Key-value-LEFT_ALT"></a>

### LEFT_ALT

`LEFT_ALT` 

The left Alt key; [`UI.isAltKeyDown`](/reference/ui/ui/#UI-method-isAltKeyDown) tests both Alt keys.

<a id="Key-value-LEFT_SUPER"></a>

### LEFT_SUPER

`LEFT_SUPER` 

The left system key: Windows on a PC, Command on a Mac, where text fields use it for their shortcuts.

<a id="Key-value-RIGHT_SHIFT"></a>

### RIGHT_SHIFT

`RIGHT_SHIFT` 

The right Shift key.

<a id="Key-value-RIGHT_CONTROL"></a>

### RIGHT_CONTROL

`RIGHT_CONTROL` 

The right Control key.

<a id="Key-value-RIGHT_ALT"></a>

### RIGHT_ALT

`RIGHT_ALT` 

The right Alt key, AltGr on many layouts.

<a id="Key-value-RIGHT_SUPER"></a>

### RIGHT_SUPER

`RIGHT_SUPER` 

The right system key: Windows on a PC, Command on a Mac.

<a id="Key-value-MENU"></a>

### MENU

`MENU` 

The context menu key.

<a id="Key-value-UNKNOWN"></a>

### UNKNOWN

`UNKNOWN` 

A key that the window library reports and JOID does not name.

---

<small>`fluent` returns the instance, typed for chaining · `factory` creates an instance · `signal` also accepts a value that follows signals, as a signal, an expression or a lambda ([When does JOID compute this value again?](/use/learn/interactivity/signals/#ask-when-does-joid-compute-this-value-again)) · `hook` called by JOID, override it · `abstract` you implement it · `default` interface method with a body · `static` called on the class · `protected` visible to subclasses</small>
